result.details:
Target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895 fetched and checked out detached under /tmp/rev41 (git rev-parse HEAD confirmed). /workspace/repo left at its assigned baseline 5672ead, clean, no source changes.

F1 MEDIUM src/cli.ts:247,249-264. reportConfigShow awaits resolveClientSettings before the guarded block, so only invalid_config (server value validation) degrades to the JSON {server:{ok:false,code,message,hint}} form. Reproduced empty-stdout exit=1 for: a typo'd key in [server], malformed TOML, env_file="missing.env", a non-assignment line in an env file, client.url=ftp://..., and SWARMFORGE_CONFIG=<absent>. Test gap: the only covering test uses a valid document with an incomplete server, the single guarded code path.

F2 MEDIUM src/cli.ts:235. env_files comes only from the --env-file flags; the document's env_file is read solely in prepare() (src/settings/load.ts:751-758), which config path never calls. Reproduced: config path --config withenvfile.toml -> {"exists":true,"env_files":[]} while secrets.env is absent and config validate then exits 1. Contradicts src/cli.ts:209-210 and README.md:77. Fix: prepend the declared env_file (anchored at the config file's directory) and add per-entry existence flags, or correct the help text.

F3 MEDIUM src/cli.ts:195 vs src/serve.ts:161,163-166. Reproduced: a database whose settings.instance_id='blue' against instance_id="green", and a live holder of the flock on <db>.lock; both returned exit=0 {"ok":true":...}. docs/SERVE.md:33-34 and docs/CONFIGURATION.md:225-226 name both as rules a serve command must keep. Fix: read-only instance_id comparison and a non-blocking flock probe inside the check-config branch.

F4 MEDIUM src/cli.ts:273. reportValidation never resolves client settings, so client.url=ftp://... yields exit=0 ok:true. config show does detect it but only by aborting with no stdout (F1), so no command reports it structurally.

F5 LOW src/cli.ts:234. existsSync with no regular-file test; --config <dir> reports exists:true, while config validate then fails EISDIR.

Cleared after probing: no filesystem side effects from any of these commands; file::memory:, :MEMORY: and file::memory:?cache=shared all create real on-disk files under bun:sqlite, so the ':memory:' refusal cannot be side-stepped, and ' :memory: ' is trimmed and refused; redaction held for every synthetic canary.

Limitations: serve was never executed, so F1-F4 rest on real CLI runs plus a source-level trace into src/serve.ts/src/runtime.ts. Whole suite not run; no packaging compiled. Artifacts sanitized through Redactor from src/security.ts at the target.
